dl008_count_resolution.methodology: String-aware brace-matched object extraction (500 objects → 500 unique QIDs). For each object, CorrectChoice extracted from within the same object as ExplanationWrong fields. No forward-scan/back-scan offset — within-object extraction is immune to CC-position variation.

discrepancy_explanation.s700_claim_342: OVERCOUNT — DL-029 forward-scan artifact. In Pack D, CorrectChoice is positioned BEFORE QuestionID in the JSON object. S700 used Select-String with forward-scan (searching from QuestionID forward to find CorrectChoice), which systematically grabs the NEXT item's CC instead of the current item's (since forward-scan misses the CC that precedes the QID). With 500 items and CC distributed A/B/C/D approximately evenly, the error rate is ~75%, producing ~340-375 false positives. This mechanism was independently confirmed: Agent C's v1 scan (forward-scan from QID) also produced 327 results before the methodology was corrected to within-object extraction.
discrepancy_explanation.session_status_claim_10: UNDERCOUNT — SESSION_STATUS was directionally correct for the items it checked but missed 10 additional DL-008 items. Specifically, SESSION_STATUS correctly identified 11 of 20 DL-008 items (AD-047/048/054/055, BD-017/021/022/023/024, DD-028/029, and flagged BD-057/058/059) but missed Section C items (CD-002/003/006/022/023/034) and some Section B items (BD-057/058/059 were flagged but 3 escaped). Section-wise, SESSION_STATUS had 0 Section C coverage and only partial Section B coverage. Additionally flagged BD-001 as DL-008 but BD-001 is CLEAN (CC=A, EW_A="").
discrepancy_explanation.governance_register_claim_1: FALSE POSITIVE — BD-001 is structurally CLEAN. CorrectChoice=A, ExplanationWrongA="". Line 3871 confirms EW_A is empty string. The governance register incorrectly flagged this item.

dl008_count_resolution.root_cause_of_discrepancy: Pack D stores CorrectChoice BEFORE QuestionID in the JSON object — the inverse of Packs A/C/E where CC follows QID. All forward-scan tools (Select-String searching from QID forward) that don't account for this order systematically grab the next item's CC, producing a ~75% false-positive DL-008 count. Only within-object extraction (brace-matched boundaries) or backward-scan yields correct results. The BD-095 missing comma additionally blocks all JavaScript parse methods (require/Function/eval), making Pack D uniquely difficult to scan with traditional tools.
